content.title: About
content.content: Shelf‑stable wheat flour tortilla is a thin, flexible flatbread made from whole‑grain wheat flour, water, salt, and sometimes a small amount of fat. It remains safe at room temperature and is ideal for quick preparation of Mexican‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat tortillas appeared in North America in the 19th century as an alternative to corn tortillas.
Traditionally the dough is rolled by hand, but industrial production uses automated rollers.
Wheat tortillas are softer and more elastic than corn, making them perfect for wraps and burritos.
Shelf‑stable versions are packaged in airtight bags that keep them fresh for up to 12 months.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat flour provides slow‑release energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: A tortilla offers about 6 g of protein per 100 g, beneficial for vegetarians.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tortillas without added oil contain less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although low in fat, tortillas provide about 250 kcal per 100 g, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tortillas for burritos, tacos, quesadillas, or as a base for no‑bake pizza. Warm them on a dry skillet, in the microwave, or in the oven. For extra softness, lightly mist with water before heating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly or transfer to an airtight container. For storage longer than six months, refrigeration is recommended.
